insight: In May 2026 Canner froze the AGPL GenBI app at v1-final and rebuilt Wren AI as an Apache-2.0 'open context layer' for agents.
name: Wren AI
tagline: Open-source GenBI agent: ask in plain language, get governed SQL, charts, and dashboards.
description: An agentic GenBI platform from Canner that turns natural-language questions into governed SQL, charts, and live dashboards over 20+ databases and warehouses, from BigQuery and Snowflake to PostgreSQL and DuckDB. Its open-source core is a semantic 'context layer' (MDL) that grounds LLM-generated queries in business definitions instead of raw schemas. Runs self-hosted via Docker or as a managed cloud with RBAC and row/column-level security.

modelSupport.notes: LLM-agnostic — bring any provider key (LiteLLM-based in the v1 app); OpenAI models are the best-tested.

edge: Self-hostable Apache-2.0 GenBI with a semantic layer that grounds agent SQL across 20+ databases — where Genie, Julius, and Hex are closed SaaS.
pros: Self-host via Docker or use managed cloud
Semantic layer grounds SQL, cuts hallucination
Many warehouses and databases via one engine
cons: 2026 pivot froze the original GenBI UI at v1
Best-tested on OpenAI; other models less so
RBAC, auditing, row-level security are paid
Docs split between v1 app and new core
